findings.evidence: `rg -n "loopDeck|deckFundamentalGroupEquiv"` finds both APIs in this file, but the only characterization at lines 116–126 mentions abstract monodromy and never relates them.
findings.fix: Add a convention-correct `@[simp]` lemma for `(deckFundamentalGroupEquiv x₀).symm (MulOpposite.op g)` in terms of `loopDeck` (and any required universal-cover monodromy/action lemma).
findings.issue: `deckFundamentalGroupEquiv` has no theorem identifying its inverse on `op g` with the explicit `loopDeck`, so consumers cannot use the advertised isomorphism as the bundled action without reconstructing the monodromy argument.

findings.evidence: Lines 58–60 and 91–93 are public `[simp]` characterization lemmas, and `Homeomorph.ext` makes `loopDeck_apply` extensional for the bundled deck transformation.
findings.fix: Remove both `@[expose]` annotations and retain the existing application lemmas as the supported API.
findings.issue: `loopDeck` and `loopDeckHom` (line 84) are marked `@[expose]` although their public behavior is already given by `loopDeck_apply` and `loopDeckHom_apply`; this unnecessarily makes constructor-level implementations part of the interface.

summary: The public equivalence is not connected to the explicit loop-deck construction, and two definitions expose bodies despite having characteristic lemmas.
